page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server provision incorporates 8 vCPUs sourced from 4 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, using 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration totals 64.0 GB of RAM, presenting a high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU features 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support including AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and has no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results situate the E8s_v5 primarily within average performance tiers for its hardware category. Stress-ng scores show 1,898.68 for single-core and 7,757.61 for multi-core performance, while Geekbench yields a single-core score of 1,657.0 and a multi-core score of 6,161.0. The memory subsystem records read bandwidths of 419.65 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 59.3 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside 42.73 GB/sec write bandwidth. In application benchmarks, the instance achieves 7.97 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 12.32 GB/sec. Deficiencies emerge in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (31.98 GB/sec) and heavy LLM text generation, where the 7B model reaches 8.58 tokens per second and the 70B prompt processing drops to 5.84 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance relies on remote Premium Storage options for persistent disk requirements, introducing external storage attachment tradeoffs. Its substantial 64.0 GB memory footprint relative to 8 vCPUs provides efficient density for memory-bound applications without necessitating over-provisioning of compute resources. The configuration suits in-memory caches, relational database systems, enterprise software deployments, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
